title: Cocktail 2 Closes at Rs 166 Crore Worldwide as Shahid Kapoor Scores Career-Best Opening
excerpt: The Homi Adajania sequel earned nearly three times its budget, giving Bollywood its sixth-highest grosser of 2026.
body:
• Cocktail 2 closed its theatrical run with a worldwide gross of Rs 166.29 crore, including Rs 104.53 crore net from Indian cinemas
  • The sequel earned nearly three times its estimated Rs 60 crore production budget, making it a profitable theatrical success despite mixed reviews
  • Shahid Kapoor delivered his highest-grossing opening ever, while Kriti Sanon notched her fourth-highest career gross
  • The film is Bollywood's sixth-highest grossing release of 2026, behind Sikandar, War 2, Sky Force, Kesari 2, and Deva

A Sequel That Found Its Audience

https://youtube.com/watch?v=XXxUqLHq1xg

Cocktail 2 wrapped its theatrical run this week with a worldwide gross of Rs 166.29 crore, cementing its place as one of Bollywood's more reliable commercial performers of 2026. The Homi Adajania-directed sequel to the 2012 original earned Rs 104.53 crore net from Indian cinemas and an additional Rs 61.76 crore from overseas and domestic gross adjustments, comfortably crossing the profitability threshold against its estimated Rs 60 crore production budget.

The film opened to Rs 12.35 crore on its first day, the biggest opening of Shahid Kapoor's career, and crossed Rs 100 crore worldwide by its first Tuesday. But Cocktail 2 was not a runaway hit. Its day-over-day drops in the first week were steep, and the second weekend brought only modest recovery, suggesting the film was front-loaded with fans and curiosity viewers rather than building through word-of-mouth.

Star Performances Drive the Numbers

Shahid Kapoor, Kriti Sanon, and Rashmika Mandanna headlined a cast that proved bankable even when reviews were divided. Kapoor had not delivered a theatrical hit of this scale since Kabir Singh in 2019, and the Rs 166 crore global total represents a significant course correction after the underperformance of Jersey and the mixed reception of Teri Baaton Mein Aisa Uljha Jiya.

For Kriti Sanon, Cocktail 2 is now her fourth-highest grossing film, trailing only Dilwale, Bareilly Ki Barfi, and Luka Chuppi.

Rashmika Mandanna, who has established herself as a pan-India star after Pushpa 2 and Animal, added another commercially successful title to her filmography. The three-way dynamic between the leads, echoing the original Cocktail's love triangle with Saif Ali Khan, Deepika Padukone, and Diana Penty, was cited by audiences as the film's strongest draw.

Where It Ranks in 2026

Cocktail 2 slots in as Bollywood's sixth-highest grosser of 2026, behind Salman Khan's Sikandar, the Hrithik Roshan-led War 2, Akshay Kumar's Sky Force, Kesari 2, and Deva. The film outperformed several bigger-budget releases that launched in the same quarter, suggesting that mid-budget Bollywood titles with the right star pairing can still find an audience in a market increasingly dominated by franchise tentpoles and South Indian crossovers.

Its overseas performance — particularly in the UK, Australia, and North American markets with large Indian diaspora populations — tracked in line with other Bollywood rom-coms, which tend to perform disproportionately well in NRI circuits compared to action or thriller genres.

The Road to OTT

With its theatrical window now closed, Cocktail 2 is expected to premiere on a major streaming platform within the next four to six weeks. OTT rights were reportedly sold pre-release, which factored into the film's break-even math. For T-Series and producer Bhushan Kumar, the film represents a clean profit on a mid-range investment, the kind of outcome that keeps the Bollywood theatrical business viable between tentpole releases.
